chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, who said: 'Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen narrated to me, saying: I asked a virtuous one (peace be upon him) about the Qunut in the Witr and Fajr prayers, and what is recited aloud in it, before the Ruku' or after it. So he (peace be upon him) said: Before the Ruku', when you finish your recitation.'
ai.seo_question: When exactly should the Qunut be recited in the Witr and Fajr prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the preferred timing for the Qunut supplication in Witr and Fajr prayers, specifying that it occurs after the completion of Quranic recitation but before entering Ruku'. In Shia jurisprudence, this timing is significant as it distinguishes the supplication as an integral part of the prayer's recitation phase rather than a post-prayer du'a, reflecting the scholarly consensus on its placement within the unit of prayer.
